question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR’s durable local restart-audit storage boundary: a shared SQLite table with fixed 512-row retention, redacted session/sensitive fields, and stored source/preflight metadata around restart scheduling and emission?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a mechanical patch defect; it is a product/security acceptance decision about persistent operational metadata plus a current-main conflict that must be resolved before the accepted boundary can merge.

options.title: Accept the restart audit contract
options.body: Merge after conflict resolution if maintainers accept the new table, fixed retention, redaction rules, and restart-path persistence as the desired local operator audit model.

options.title: Narrow persisted metadata first
options.body: Require a smaller column/payload set or stricter privacy tests if the current source/preflight/client metadata boundary is too broad.

options.title: Defer to broader audit design
options.body: Pause this PR if restart audit rows should wait for a unified audit-ledger direction instead of landing as a restart-specific producer now.

recommendation.title: Accept the restart audit contract
recommendation.body: Merge after conflict resolution if maintainers accept the new table, fixed retention, redaction rules, and restart-path persistence as the desired local operator audit model.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass points to steipete for both shared SQLite state and gateway restart tracing, and the decision is about their intersection with security-sensitive audit storage.
